brief_description: RFP for Chemical analyses of marine sediment samples for determination of specified drugs, pesticides, and antibiotics concentrations Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) collects sediment samples to assess the far-field environmental effects of marine aquaculture on the East and West coasts of Canada. Samples collected at near-, mid-, and far-field locations are analyzed for concentrations of a defined suite of drugs, pesticides, and antibiotics, as well as moisture content. DFO is assessing the presence and ecological significance of aquaculture-related chemical compounds in far field environments. As DFO lacks in house capacity for these analyses, a qualified laboratory is required. The term of any resulting contract is for Contract Award issuance to September 29, 2027, but Canada may extend the term for up to four (4) additional one-year option periods, to September 29, 2031.

organization: Department of Public Works and Government Services (PSPC)
brief_description: The Carabobo is a former Flower-class corvette built in 1940–1941 that sank in 1945 after running aground in Gaspé Bay during transit to Venezuela. The wreck lies at a depth of just under ten metres, with an intact stern section and scattered structural remnants spread over a wide, undefined area on the seabed near Forillon National Park.The Canadian Coast Guard first responded to reported leaks in 2000–2001, recovering oil and securing the wreck. In 2019, additional reports of oil bubbles prompted a diver inspection, which confirmed that the wreck is highly degraded and heavily covered in algae, making visual assessment difficult. The primary risk associated with the Carabobo wreck is environmental, particularly the potential for intermittent releases of residual hydrocarbons or contaminated sediments. brief_description: Calou - The port side is submerged at high tide. There are multiple hull breaches resulting in water ingress; the starboard side has collapsed and the starboard bow is severely torn. The wreck is unsafe, with numerous sharp hazards and unrestricted public access. The vessel has a slight starboard list, and the hull is in an advanced state of deterioration. The deck is severely damaged, with large openings and multiple points of water ingress. Wilcox – The keel is broken, and the hull is sagging. The structure is severely deteriorated, with numerous unstable sections. It is heeled over on the port side, with a central point of structural collapse. The port side hull is partially buried under a layer of fine rock. The stern remains largely intact, while the bow is destroyed. The level of decay is advanced. Water flows freely through the structure at high tide. title: 5P468-26-0011/A Stage 2 - Johnston Canyon Rock Slope Remediation, Banff National Park
brief_description: 5P468-26-0011/A Stage 2- Johnston Canyon Rock Slope Remediation, Banff National Park REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency requires the services of a qualified contractor to complete rock slope remediation work along the Johnston Canyon Trail in Banff National Park. The work is part of Parks Canada’s ongoing rockfall hazard management that is intended to reduce the potential safety hazards along the busy trail which runs through the narrow, vertical walled canyon. The work will be situated in a remote environment with significant access and logistical constraints. The scope of work includes but is not limited to rock scaling, trimming, rock bolt and rock dowel installations. Access to the site is restricted to pedestrian and small ATV means, with limited vehicular access and very limited on-site staging or laydown areas. All construction activities, materials, and equipment must be transported to and from the site using existing trail networks and/or helicopter-supported access, requiring careful planning and coordination to safely and efficiently execute the work within a sensitive national park environment. title: Bio-capacitance probe system
brief_description: Acquisition of a new four-probe system enabling real-time measurement of bio-capacitance for cell culture in bioreactors, for up to four bioreactors in parallel. This system will enable real-time estimation of viable cell concentration in those bioreactors. Measuring bio-capacitance at multiple frequencies, at regular intervals, in order to obtain the capacitance distribution spectrum of the cells, thereby enabling the real-time calculation of other critical cell culture parameters such as cell size, internal cell conductivity, and critical frequency. The probes to be acquired under this procurement must be compatible with the different types of bioreactors used by the team. In addition, the selected bio-capacitance probes must allow multi-frequency scanning for real-time determination of the intrinsic dielectric properties of the cells through analysis of the ß-dispersion of the signal using the Cole–Cole a model. Finally, the generated data must be capable of being captured in real time both by the control and data acquisition system via OPC-UA communication, and via 4–20 mA communication to enable integration of the probe directly into a control loop.

title: Chartering an oceanographic research vessel and crew, Fall Mission – Atlantic Zone Monitoring Program (AZMP)
brief_description: The objective of the Atlantic Zone Monitoring Program (AZMP) is to monitor oceanographic conditions in the Atlantic Ocean on an annual basis. For over 25 years, Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has been conducting regular monitoring of the Estuary and Gulf of St. Lawrence to document variations in physical, chemical and biological properties (e.g., temperature, salinity, primary production). This work is usually carried out aboard Canadian Coast Guard (CCG) vessels. DFO wishes to charter an oceanographic research vessel (other than a CCG vessel) to carry out the AZMP fall survey in the Estuary and Gulf of St. Lawrence. The survey aims to collect data to better understand, describe and predict the state of the marine ecosystem, as well as to quantify changes in chemical, physical and biological properties.

organization: Department of Public Works and Government Services (PSPC)
brief_description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), in collaboration with the Public Health Agency of Canada and Health Emergency Readiness Canada (HERC), is seeking stakeholder input to inform the application of the Policy in federally managed vaccine procurement. brief_description: Canada, as represented by the Department of National Defence (DND), with the assistance of Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), has issued this RFI on the Dive Tender Replacement (DTR) project. This RFI is seeking Industry feedback regarding potential solutions which meet the Dive Tender Replacement project operational requirements as listed in Annex A provided herewith. The DTR build requirement is anticipated to fall under the small vessel construction component, Pillar 2, of the National Shipbuilding Strategy (NSS). Restrictions-on-bidding provisions may therefore, apply to the shipyards selected by Canada under Pillar 1 of the NSS. The Royal Canadian Navy (RCN) currently uses an existing fleet of Granby and Sechelt-class vessels to support divers in completing underwater tasks that are essential to naval operations and public safety. The new vessels aim to replace the existing fleet of Granby and Sechelt-class vessels, to facilitate the full range of diving operations and will resemble traditional 24-crew diving support vessels.

title: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada - Interpreter Program
brief_description: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) is Canada's largest independent administrative tribunal. It is responsible for making well-reasoned decisions on immigration and refugee matters, efficiently, fairly and in accordance with the law. The IRB decides, among other responsibilities, who needs refugee protection among the thousands of claimants who come to Canada annually. Every year, the Board renders thousands of decisions on refugee protection and immigration matters. At these hearings, refugees and immigrants who are not fluent in English or French count on the IRB to provide them with interpretive services. These interpretive services are required in a wide variety of languages and dialects, reflecting the diverse backgrounds of the refugees and immigrants who come to Canada. In order to manage the interpretive services required for such a large number of hearings, including urgent hearings, IRB issues contracts to interpreters who provide services on an “as-and-when-requested” basis and invoice for any services they provide. An SA is a non-binding arrangement between Canada and a pre-qualified supplier that allows departments and agencies to award contracts and solicit bids from a pool of pre-qualified suppliers for specific requirements within the scope of the SA. An SA is not a contract for the provision of goods and services described in it and neither party is legally bound, as a result of signing a supply arrangement alone. The intent of a supply arrangement is to establish a framework to permit expeditious processing of individual bid solicitations, which result in legally binding contracts for the goods and services described in those bid solicitations.
